<meta>continues from previous page: ...to our hearts' content,</meta>

**EUBULUS.** What birds do I see here? **CATHARINA.** It is the patriarch of the college. Do not withdraw; they have already finished drinking; sit down for a little while; once he has departed, we shall chat in our usual way. **EUBULUS.** Come, I will grant you what you were unwilling to tell me. Now that we are alone, tell the whole story, for I would prefer to learn it from you. **CATHARINA.** Out of so many friends, whom I thought very highly of, I now realize there was none who gave me more prudent or mature advice than you, the youngest of all. **EUBULUS.** But how did you overcome your parents' affection? **CATHARINA.** First, by the persistent exhortations of the monks and nuns: then by my own: my mother’s mind was shaken by prayers and flatteries: my father could in no way be driven to it. At last, after applying every engine of persuasion, he was conquered and overwhelmed rather than consenting. It was done over drinks: they threatened a horrible, fatal evil if he denied Christ his bride. **EUBULUS.** O the wickedness of those fools! What happened then? **CATHARINA.** I was kept secretly at home for three days: meanwhile, several women of that college, whom they call the Converted <note>Latin: *Conversas*; lay sisters or women living under a religious rule without full vows</note>, were always present, adding spirit through their encouragements so that I might persist in my holy purpose, and taking anxious care lest any of my kinswomen or companions might come to me, who seemed likely to change my mind. Meanwhile, garments and other things pertaining to the feast were being prepared. **EUBULUS.** What was your state of mind meanwhile? Were you wavering? **CATHARINA.** No, but I suffered something so horrendous that I would rather die ten times over than endure it again. **EUBULUS.** I pray you, what is that? **CATHARINA.** I cannot speak of it. **EUBULUS.** Whatever you say to me, you say to your friend. **CATHARINA.** Do you promise silence? **EUBULUS.** I would have maintained it even if you had not made it a condition. As if you do not know me yet.

<summary>Catharina recounts how she was pressured into the convent through the manipulative tactics of monks and nuns who intimidated her father. She describes being isolated from her family and friends by lay sisters to ensure she did not change her mind before the ceremony.</summary>

<keywords>Catharina, Eubulus, monasticism, parental consent, religious manipulation, lay sisters, secrecy, persuasion</keywords>
